title: Digital Storytelling as a 21st Century Pedagogical Strategy
content: Digital storytelling is an emerging pedagogical strategy whereby the traditional art of storytelling is merged with modern technologies and multimedia, where learners construct narratives through combinations of storylines, images, sound, audio, video, animation, music, and texts. As modern education systems emphasize such skills as creativity, communication, collaboration, critical thinking, digital literacy, and learner autonomy, there are plenty of opportunities for integration of these skills within digital storytelling. This paper explores digital storytelling as a pedagogical strategy of the 21st century and discusses its theoretical background, features, educational application, advantages, and difficulties of implementation. The analysis shows that digital storytelling can be a very helpful tool for active, collaborative, experiential, and student-centered learning. It also considers the importance of digital storytelling for the development of multiliteracy and multimodality, as well as its applicability in the context of contemporary teacher education and technologically enhanced learning environment. The paper concludes that digital storytelling should not be considered just a technological exercise, but a pedagogical strategy where learners construct knowledge and communication skills, reflect their experiences, and critically evaluate digital media.
